objectives: Spell familiar CVC words containing p.
Map each spoken phoneme to its corresponding grapheme.
Self-check p-containing spellings by reading them back.
concepts: Encoding reverses the decoding direction: spoken phonemes are mapped to written graphemes.
The position of /p/ determines where p appears in the written word.
Segmenting provides the ordered sequence needed for spelling.

definitions.definition: Using known sound-letter relationships to write spoken words.
Writing a word after hearing it spoken.

commonMistakes: Writing p in the wrong position.
Writing without first segmenting the word.

basic: Spell pat, map and tap from dictation.
conceptual: Identify the phoneme represented by each letter in a p-containing CVC word.
higherOrderThinking: Diagnose whether an encoding error is initial, medial or final.
mixedReview: Segment, map, write and check CVC words with p.

mistakeBasedRevision: If p is misplaced, say the word slowly and identify where /p/ occurs.
weakTopicRevision: Dictate short p-containing CVC words and repeat only words with sound-to-letter errors.

activities.name: Sound-to-letter dictation
steps: Learner writes one grapheme per sound.

activities.name: Build and spell
steps: Build a word with letter cards.

outcomes: Learner spells at least 8 of 10 familiar p-containing CVC words correctly from dictation.
Learner places p accurately in initial or final position.
Learner self-checks spelling by reading the written word back.

questions.question: What should you do before writing a CVC word you hear?
Which letter should be written for /p/?
A learner spells 'pat' as 'sat'. Which sound needs checking?
A learner spells 'map' as 'mat'. Which sound needs checking?
Which word has p as its first letter?
Which word has p as its final letter?
Why should the learner segment before spelling?
options: It gives the ordered sound sequence to map to letters
It removes the need to listen

questions.question: Which activity best practises /p/ spelling?
options: Dictate pat, map and tap and have the learner segment and write them

questions.question: What should the learner do after spelling a word?
options: Read it back and check each sound

questions.question: Which spelling shows correct p mapping?
What shows secure /p/ encoding?
options: The learner spells familiar CVC words with p accurately from dictation
The learner only identifies p visually
